views.name: Phase 1 delivery tooling flow
views.view_type: process flow (flowchart TB) with artifact-derivation lane
views.question: How does every entry point reach one Phase 1 gate (spec, docs, hygiene), when does vnv-review run, and how does the shared spec-authoring skill reach this repo's spec gate area while D1 waits for spec-track assembly (ST-4)?
views.concern: One verdict for local, CI and harness runs; workflow safety (C14); vnv typed gap (C12); hook ordering (C13); private-to-public vendoring of D5; rule 12 hygiene; Phase 1 tooling / spec-track and Phase 2 boundary.
views.rationale: D4 and D5 are tooling deliverables with many entry points and one shared resource (Alphazedehq skills/ tree); a flow view shows the single gate, the vendoring seam, and what Phase 2 adds.
views.abstraction: Artifact and step level; no per-harness hook mechanics (deferred to Planning and Design); no workflow YAML. Spec-track content (D1) and Phase 2 content (android/backend areas) are shown dashed, not designed.
views.interpretation: Git hooks, Actions (pull_request plus push to main) and harness hooks (via Alphazedehq:hooks/ci-gate-hook.sh) all call tools/ci/gate.sh AREA (spec, docs, hygiene); Phase 2 adds android and backend behind the same entrypoint. ship-pull-request runs vnv-review when a guidance tree exists (this repo: S07 docs/vnv/ with ci-cd, spec, developer-feedback), else REFUSED_NO_VNV (never a pass). D5 generalizes the GridMarket kit into Alphazedehq:skills/spec-authoring/, the S42 vendor step copies its scripts to tools/spec/, and the spec area lints and rebuilds each spec/<name>/ or self-checks the vendored template while none exists. D1 is a dashed spec-track consumer (ST-4). SD-013 (copy GridMarket kit) is superseded and not shown.
views.supported_decision: D4/D5 file layout, lane order (C13), the spec gate area contents, and the boundary between Phase 1 tooling and its spec-track and Phase 2 consumers.
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are provisional until the Requirements Engineer Phase 1 PASS. REFUSED_NO_VNV terminal does not model whether merge proceeds in repos without a guidance tree (OD-AFC-10 recommends a non-pass row). vnv-review also accepts Vnv/AGENTS.md.
views.canonical_source: views/v4-delivery-tooling.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions

views.name: Phase 1 context and boundary
views.view_type: context block view (flowchart LR with nested repo boundary)
views.question: What is inside the Phase 1 tooling boundary, which external actors and systems does it touch, and where are the trust boundaries?
views.concern: Phase 1 scope (tooling only, no product); private Alphazedehq vs public repo seam; hosted-runner budget (C11); hook ordering (C13); secrets and local paths (C7, C14).
views.rationale: A boundary view is the cheapest way to fix the Phase 1 tooling scope and its trust seams before allocation.
views.abstraction: Repository and skill level; no per-file layout (see design.md), no workflow YAML, no hook mechanics.
views.interpretation: This repo holds the gate (spec, docs, hygiene), hooks, workflow, vendored tools/spec/, the Vnv tree and the Scribe log. Alphazedehq skills author the gate and workflow and vendor D5; GridMarket is the read-only D5 source. Agents commit through local or harness hooks; Actions runs ci.yml on hosted runners. The spec track (ST-4 D1) and Phase 2 (android/backend areas) consume the vendored tools and the gate.
views.supported_decision: Phase 1 scope boundary and interface ownership (D4/D5 vs repo artifacts vs spec track and Phase 2).
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are provisional until the Requirements Engineer Phase 1 PASS. The vnv-review skill and the harnesses are external actors; their internals are not modeled. RISK-AFC-07 (route limits) and RISK-AFC-08 (exhausted minutes) are process controls, not drawn.
views.canonical_source: views/v5-phase1-context.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions

views.name: Phase 1 use cases and outcomes
views.view_type: use-case view (rounded capsules in SVG; stadium nodes in Mermaid)
views.question: Which tooling goals do agents and the owner achieve with the Phase 1 deliverables, and what observable outcome ends each?
views.concern: Agent-visible behaviour of D4/D5; identical gate verdicts; honest typed gaps; verified repo setup.
views.rationale: Outcome capsules give the Requirements Engineer and Test Engineer a verifiable end state per tooling goal.
views.abstraction: Goal level; no commands beyond the contract names; no product behaviour.
views.interpretation: UC-T1 ends in a lint-clean built spec with byte-identical rebuild. UC-T2 ends in a PASS or typed FAIL/GAP identical from every entry point. UC-T3 ends in a gate table with findings (or REFUSED_NO_VNV) and a rebase/merge-commit landing. UC-T4 ends in a wired gate plus workflow plus hooks verified by a deliberate failing change.
views.supported_decision: Tooling acceptance outcomes and V&V scenarios per Phase 1 deliverable.
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are provisional until the Requirements Engineer Phase 1 PASS. Product use cases are out of Phase 1 scope; MODEL-AFC-V2 stays the spec-track reference.
views.canonical_source: views/v6-phase1-use-cases.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions

views.name: Context and trust boundaries
views.view_type: context block view (flowchart LR with nested boundaries)
views.question: What is inside the system boundary, which external actors and systems does it touch, and where are the trust boundaries?
views.concern: Scope boundary, hosting on shared resources (one Fire TV stick, one AWS account), secret handling, untrusted input, launch safety.
views.rationale: A boundary view is the cheapest way to fix system scope and the four trust boundaries before requirements are allocated.
views.abstraction: Component level; protocols named only at trust boundaries. Omits data schemas, deployment sizing, CI.
views.interpretation: tv-app/ and backend/ are the system. TB1 HTTPS with per-device bearer token; TB2 Yahoo tokens and client secret server-side only (SSM SecureString); TB3 ESPN responses untrusted and validated at ingest; TB4 provider launch by explicit intent to allow-listed packages. Alexa is optional (C8).
views.supported_decision: Requirement allocation per component and trust boundary; interface requirements for TB1..TB4.
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are not final until the Requirements Engineer passes. Provider app is a placeholder until spike SP-3 picks one. Phase 1 update: this product view is superseded by the spec-track (ST-3) sysml-v2 models; it is kept as spec-track reference input, not D5/D4 design.
views.canonical_source: views/v1-context.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions

views.name: Operational flow
views.question: How does a live game event become a heads-up alert and a provider launch, how does the panel refresh, and where does Mode B fall back to Mode A?
views.concern: End-to-end behaviour, fallbacks (C2 replay, C5 Mode A, C6 manual lineup), suppression and correction handling, launch outcome truthfulness.
views.rationale: The alert path crosses both systems and three trust boundaries; a flow view exposes every decision a requirement must cover.
views.abstraction: Step level; no timing values beyond spike_panel_max; long-poll and refresh intervals are unset.
views.interpretation: ESPN poll -> validate (else labeled replay) -> normalize/dedupe/corrections -> match against starters -> policy -> /v1/alerts long-poll -> heads-up notification -> Watch -> resolver -> explicit intent -> typed launch outcome. Panel path GET /v1/panel -> PanelService -> render with stale marks. SP-4 verdict picks Mode B or Mode A.
views.supported_decision: Behavioural requirements, fault behaviour, and V&V scenarios (replay, suppression, each launch outcome, each panel mode).
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are not final until the Requirements Engineer passes. No timing budgets (owner: lightweight design, no benchmarks). Phase 1 update: this product view is superseded by the spec-track (ST-3) sysml-v2 models; it is kept as spec-track reference input, not D5/D4 design.
views.canonical_source: views/v3-operational-flow.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions
